title: Significance of small axial hiatal hernias and moderate forms of esophagitis before and after bariatric surgery: New scoring system to aid decision-making regarding simultaneous hiatal repair during bariatric surgery
summary:
It is still unclear which patients truly benefit from simultaneous hiatal hernia repair during bariatric surgery (pHHR). There is a lack of reliable algorithms and underlying evidence in this area. As a result, this decision is handled very differently in practice and is discussed accordingly at conferences.
In our opinion, the issue is equally unclear for sleeve gastrectomies as it is for gastric bypass surgeries, especially mini gastric bypasses, as well as for follow-up bariatric surgeries, i.e., secondary hiatal hernia repairs (sHHR).
While larger findings are generally easier to decide on in terms of treatment, i.e., pHHR or sHHR, the “minor” findings from the respective preoperative gastroscopies, such as hiatal hernia 1-3 cm and esophagitis grade Los Angeles classification A/B (or 0/1 according to Savary-Miller), which are common in bariatric patients and must be interpreted in the context of clinical data and other questionnaires (RSI, LQ). 
We want to change this and objectify it to a certain extent by specifying parameters in the form of a new, simple (semi-quantitative) scoring system.
To this end, a retrospective analysis using the study outlined here will be conducted to determine whether such a score may be suitable for supporting the indication for pHHR by applying it retroactively and then comparing it with the actual courses of treatment.
Approximately 500 patients are expected to participate in this retrospective study, which will cover three years (2020-2022) with a maximum follow-up period of 60 months (until the end of 2024).
In subsequent prospective studies (multicenter), the score will be applied in practice and validated, and then also transferred to bariatric revision surgery (sHHR).

interventions.name:
In the study, the usual basic bariatric data for all patients is retrospectively recorded in tabular form; specifically, this includes
•Age
•Gender
•Preoperative BMI (for surgical indication)
•Primary bariatric procedure (sleeve or MGB)
•Months since primary surgery (0 = preoperative)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•StuDoQ consent (national data registry of the German Society for General and Visceral Surgery, DGAV) for metabolic and bariatric procedures (MBE)
•All primary sleeves and MGBs 2020-2022 from WKK Heide, which will amount to approximately 400-500 inclusions
•Maximum follow-up period until the end of 2024
Exclusion criteria:
•Previous surgery on the stomach/diaphragm
•Under 18 and over 70 years of age
•Lack of StuDoQ consent
